text:
maya: quick sync: prototyping an evict->flowback pattern. instead of firing blind evicts that just drop cache, emit a flowback event admission can consume so it can proactively reshape the request (smaller microbatch, divert to fallback model, or delay). want early feedback before an RFC.

rahul: ok, high-level: why flowback instead of stronger eviction throttles? i'm worried about oscillations and unfair tenant behavior.

maya: main goals: 1) avoid evict->reload loops that thrash KV warmup, 2) let admission make SLA-aware choices (route premium traffic appropriately), 3) give admission richer signals than a silent LRU eviction.

lucas: KV rewarm cost is huge. i'm worried this shifts tail costs into admission time and just moves the problem. how do you prevent shifting the tail?

maya: plan: warm_grace + hysteresis + dampening on flowback. flowback carries metadata: tenant, evict_reason, last_warm_ts, deadline_hint. admission uses slab membership + hint to decide. example pseudo:

```
emit_flowback(ev) // {tenant, warm_ts, hint}
on_flowback(f) {
  s = slab_for(f.tenant)
  if s.premium && now - f.warm_ts < WARM_GRACE: ignore_eviction()
  else if f.hint < SLAB_THRESH: divert_to_small_batch()
  else accept_normal()
}
```

anya: SLA surface concern: premium routes must have deterministic behavior. we cannot silently divert them and increase latency without explicit opt-in.

maya: agreed. slab contracts: premium = strict headroom, no automatic redirect unless explicit degrade policy. mid slabs = probabilistic diversion + notification. console knobs: preemptive_divert toggle, headroom tokens per route.

rahul: metrics we should track: flowback_rate, rewarm_rate, kv_miss_delta, p90/p95/p99 by slab, fairness (Jain), tenant_toggle_rate (oscillations).

lucas: rollout idea: internal-only canary on 1% hosts with synthetic hot tenants. also implement an emergency kill-switch to drop flowback path if thrash detected.

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary for branch "evict-flowback/proto" to staging at 2024-04-12T15:00Z :rocket: 

maya: test plan: 1) hot-tenant steady stream vs baseline; 2) mixed traffic with short bursts; 3) premium route under pressure. targets: rewarm overhead <10%, p95 premium <= +5%. volunteers?

anya: i'll own SLA contract surface and console flag copy.

rahul: i'll own metrics + alerts (oscillation alert + kv miss spike).

lucas: i'll build synthetic harness and run warm/cold migration tests.

maya: thanks. i'll put a short RFC in design docs and land an observe-only proto first (emit flowback, no-op consumer). iterate from metrics. tl;dr: flowback gives admission SLA context but needs warm_grace/hysteresis and careful rollout to avoid cache thrash. :white_check_mark:
